title: Acceptance
description: An acceptance record stored in acceptances/<assignment-id>/<login>.json within a PXL Classroom control repository.

assignment_id.description: ID of the assignment being accepted.

github_id.description: Immutable GitHub user ID (sender.id from the star event).

accepted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the acceptance was recorded.

star_event_ref.description: URL of the workflow run that processed the star event.

team_slug.description: URL-safe slug identifying the team if this is a group assignment.

team_name.description: Display name of the team if this is a group assignment.

status.description: Current status of the acceptance lifecycle.

claimed_email.description: The address this acceptance was admitted on, under roster_mode claim or open. Distinct from the org-scoped binding in students/claims/<github_id>.json, which can legitimately differ later after an unlink and a re-claim. Never reaches Pages.

claim_verified.description: Whether the student confirmed a GitHub-verified address rather than typing one. Evidence, never enforcement - the hub cannot check it.

claim_domain_allowed.description: Whether the address was inside claim_domains. Always true under claim, where a failing domain is refused before a record exists; under open nothing is refused, so this is the detection half.

reused_existing_repo.description: The repository already existed when this student accepted, so provisioning handed it back rather than generating from the template - they do not have this assignment's starter code. Written only when true, and only for a repository this assignment did not create: a student re-accepting leaves through the already-accepted branch, and a group member joining a teammate's repository is the assignment working. Recorded because the lecturer allowed reuse for the cohort (assignment.existing_repo_policy) and still has to be told which students it actually happened to.
